content.title: Is Kohl's closing more stores in 2026? CEO gives update
content.text: Company executives said Kohl’s is not planning another round of widespread store closures in 2026, according to comments made in a recent earnings call.“I would not anticipate any sort of grand plan of saying we’re taking stores out or adding stores at this point,” CEO Michael Bender said this month.This follows a year in which the department store chain shut down a spree of underperforming locations as part of a broader turnaround effort.Why It MattersDespite being a popular retailer across the country, Kohl’s has recently made major updates to its brick‑and‑mortar business, announcing several store closures in 2025.However, with no closings slated for 2026, the company’s business outlook has improved, and its store footprint is expected to remain largely stable in the year ahead. Entrances to a large Kohl's in Manassas, Virginia, is pictured in this undated file photo. (Getty)Kohl’s Lays Out Vision for 2026Bender said the company does not anticipate major store closures or large-scale additions in 2026, emphasizing its goal is now improved performance at existing locations rather than shrinking the chain further. “The focus for us is actually on optimizing what we already have and we’ll be focused on making sure that we continue to push the stores' productivity going forward,” Bender said.Kohl’s operates more than 1,100 stores nationwide, and company leadership has said that well over 90 percent of those are profitable.Instead of reducing its physical footprint, Kohl’s says, it is concentrating on boosting store productivity and strengthening value offerings as part of its turnaround strategy.How Many Stores Closed in 2025?While Kohl’s does not expect to close additional stores in 2026, the company did shutter 27 underperforming locations in 2025 across multiple states. Those closures were announced earlier as part of cost-cutting and restructuring efforts during a period of declining sales. After completing those shutdowns, Kohl’s leadership has indicated that the remaining store base is in a stronger financial position. What People Are SayingBender, in a statement: “In 2026, we are committed to further strengthening our foundation by addressing operational opportunities, building on our strengths, and modernizing our processes. We are confident that the work we are investing in now is essential for Kohl’s long-term benefit.”Alex Beene, financial literacy instructor for the University of Tennessee at Martin, to Newsweek last year: "While Kohl's is closing just 27 stores nationwide, a number that makes up less than three percent of its retail locations, it's easy to see why many would label this yet another event that's a sign of the times for retail. It all comes down to foot traffic at these locations, and in our current economic climate, retailers like Kohl's are more likely to close underperforming stores quickly compared to retailers in past decades."R.J. Hottovy, head of analytical research at Placer.ai, to Newsweek last year: "Kohl's decision to close 27 stores isn't particularly surprising. Over the past year, many retailers have focused on optimizing their store footprints by closing underperforming locations and reallocating resources to enhance existing stores. Additionally, population migration has shifted trade areas, making it more challenging for some locations to thrive. Notably, many of Kohl's planned closures are concentrated in California, where several markets have experienced population declines in recent years."What Happens NextBased on this month’s earnings call, the company reported improved profitability and cash flow in 2025, despite continued pressure on overall sales. Overall, net sales for the last quarter dropped about 3.9 percent and comparable store sales fell 2.8 percent.For now, executives say, the retailer will continue to review store performance annually, but no new wave of closures has been announced for 2026.“We are ending 2025 in a stronger position than we started, with important work still ahead of us,” Bender said. “Over the past year, our efforts have been focused on resetting our foundation. This focus is intended to stabilize the business and strengthen our operational ability to build for a stronger future.”
